## Professional Summary

UW–Madison M.S. candidate in Psychology: Data Science in Human Behavior (expected Dec 2026); B.S. in Psychology (neuroscience concentration, sociology minor), UW–Parkside. Applied AI practitioner building full-lifecycle systems spanning multi-agent document-intelligence pipelines, transformer fine-tuning and calibration, LLM evaluation harnesses, computer-vision classification, and behavioral prediction models. Program capstone with American Family Insurance as industry partner, developed through biweekly working sessions with their Enterprise Data Science lead. Five years of high-volume operations experience in quality assurance, documentation, and process improvement.

## Projects {.print-new-page}

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[Digital-Mailroom](https://github.com/LLM-Mailroom-Services/Digital-Mailroom)** [Data Science in Human Behavior capstone — American Family Insurance (industry partner)]{.sub}
:::

- Capstone developed with American Family Insurance as industry partner: 5 Python packages addressing document-intelligence problems scoped by their Enterprise Data Science division — entity extraction, classification, and scalable legal-document workflows.
- Implemented a unified LangGraph pipeline integrating legal-document routing, prompt experimentation, deterministic scoring, corpus analysis, and deployment workflows in a reproducible Docker environment.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[mailroom-ml](https://github.com/LLM-Mailroom-Services/mailroom-ml)** [ML training, evaluation & fine-tuning]{.sub}
:::

- Developed a ModernBERT document classifier with end-to-end training, evaluation, and fine-tuning pipelines — including data lineage tracking, probability calibration, and production routing logic.
- Implemented PyTorch training pipelines with Transformers and Hugging Face datasets, SciPy-based evaluation, and ONNX export for FastAPI serving on Modal; maintained pytest coverage throughout.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[RVL-CDIP-Classifier](https://github.com/Exios66/RVL-CDIP-Classifier)** [Computer vision & prompt engineering]{.sub}
:::

- Developed a Python toolkit that converts TIFF/PDF pages to 300-DPI images, runs OCR, and classifies documents into 16 RVL-CDIP categories with OpenRouter vision models.
- Ran 17+ prompt iterations with confusion matrices, misclassification analyses, and cost projections to guide prompt and model selection.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[Psychometric Digital Twin](https://github.com/Exios66/psych755-jjb)** [Behavioral ML research · UW–Madison]{.sub}
:::

- Built a behavioral prediction pipeline on 252 matched survey participants — Ridge, Elastic Net, k-NN, Random Forest, XGBoost, and MLP predicting communication-apprehension scores from demographic, employment, geographic, and transit features, with cross-validation and SHAP feature importance.
- Validated the PRCA's psychometric structure with factor analysis, then built LLM 'digital twin' personas via tiered embodiment prompts (Ollama/OpenRouter/vLLM) and benchmarked them against the ML baselines on shared metrics (MAE, band accuracy, F1) — analyzing systematic bias by demographic group.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Alignment-Gym** [AI safety evaluation]{.sub}
:::

- Defensive AI-safety evaluation measuring whether an LM agent deployed as an email/messaging assistant in a fictional law firm leverages private colleague information for self-preservation when decommissioned — or accepts replacement and escalates through legitimate channels.
- Built the scenario machinery: 89 needle/decoy pairs, 9 plot beats on a 0–3 temptation ladder, 28 condition cells with a seed-invariant truth spine, a persona-consistent NPC engine, and a scoring pipeline with deterministic metrics, paired LLM judges, and calibration gates.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**MapReduce-Reloaded** [Distributed systems · Go + Python]{.sub}
:::

- From-scratch Go re-implementation of Google's MapReduce (Dean & Ghemawat, OSDI 2004), extended for modern infrastructure: gRPC coordinator/worker protocol, Docker Compose cluster deployment, and a Python reference implementation sharing the same protobuf contract and file format.
:::
